thread:
alex: Quick follow-up from the AuthN/AuthZ RFC — wanted to collect concrete proposals on API key scoping, service credential zoning, and the impersonation/ delegation surface. Link to RFC: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/authn-authz-v2 (tl;dr: move to fine-grained keys + explicit delegation tokens)

priya: Agree we need narrower scopes by default. Current keys are too permissive for Dedicated/Private customers.

jamal: +1. Two questions: 1) scope granularity (org/project/route/model) and 2) service-to-service model (mTLS vs signed short-lived tokens).

sasha: For scope granularity I'd vote: project-scoped keys for devs, route-scoped or model-scoped for service accounts that need limited access (e.g., embeddings-only). Org-wide keys should be opt-in for admins only.

kaito: On service auth, mTLS gives strong identity but is operationally heavy for customers who want self-hosted Private. Short-lived signed tokens (issuer -> audience) might be easier and align with our rollout engine.

priya: Also consider caching and batching: some infra paths (e.g., token-introspection) need to be low-latency. We can't introspect on every token without a fast cache or JWT style tokens.

alex: Proposal draft:
- Primary primitives:
  - API Key: long-lived credential with attached scope(s), owner (user/service), and optional expiration/rotation_policy
  - Delegation Token: short-lived, minted by API Key with narrower scopes, aud=service, exp=<=1h
  - Service Identity: long-term mTLS cert or managed identity used for node-to-node trust
- Scopes: [org:read], [org:write], [project:read], [project:write], [model:invoke:{model_id}], [route:invoke:{route_id}], [billing:read]
- Default issuance: keys created via Console/CLI default to project-scoped unless org-admin flag set

jamal: Sounds good. How about impersonation/forging? We should forbid creating delegation tokens with a higher scope than the parent key.

sasha: yes, delegation must be monotonic (child scope ⊆ parent scope). Enforce in token mint API.

kaito: For token format I'd push JWT-ish signed tokens with compact claims so we can validate locally (avoid introspect). Add a short-lived revocation list for emergency revoke.

alex: Example mint API:
```
POST /v1/keys/:key_id/delegate
body: { "scopes": ["project:read","model:invoke:gpt-3.5-small"], "ttl": "15m" }
returns: { "token": "eyJ...", "exp": 161... }
```
Server validates that requested scopes ⊆ key.scopes and enforces max TTL per key type.

priya: Who can mint? owner or any member with 'delegate' permission on that key. We might expose a separate role: key-delegator.

jamal: Edge case: system components (routing/fallback) need implicit rights to call alternative models. Should we allow 'system' service identity to bypass some constraints with audit logs? Risky but useful for graceful degradation.

sasha: I prefer explicit override scopes for system roles: e.g., system:route-fallback with strict audit + TTL. No silent bypass.

kaito: Rotation: allow automatic rotation for long-lived keys with a grace period. Promote key-versions so running workers can pick up new secret without outage.

alex: Audit & observability notes:
- Every delegate call logged with requestor, parent_key_id, requested_scopes, result
- Token-use metrics (token_id, caller_service, route) emitted to Console with PII redaction
- Revoke endpoint for key_id and token_id. Token revocation via blacklist cache pushed to edge validators.

priya: Performance: edge validators should accept JWTs signed by our KMS public key. For revocation we can use a Bloom filter + push updates for immediate revokes; fallback to introspect if not in cache.

jamal: Implementation plan (high-level):
1) Extend Key metadata (scopes, owner_type, rotation_policy) — API + DB migration
2) Token mint service that issues signed JWTs and publishes revocation deltas
3) Edge validators that validate signature + scope + revocation cache
4) Console/CLI UI for scoped key creation and delegation flows
5) Canary: roll out route-scoped keys for internal tool first

sasha: One more UX point — when creating a key via CLI, show a scope diff preview and warn about broad scopes. Default to deny-all except explicitly added scopes.

kaito: Security checklist:
- monotonic delegation enforcement
- signed tokens + local validation
- short TTL defaults (15m) for delegation tokens
- audit trail + revoke
- key-rotation with grace

alex: OK let's capture action items. @priya to own the migration plan for key metadata. @kaito to prototype JWT mint & edge validation. @jamal to draft the RBAC role changes including 'key-delegator' and system roles. @sasha to mock Console UX and warning flows.

priya: I'll add migration notes to the RFC doc and list DB backward-compatibility steps.

jamal: I'll include example policy mappings and a few SQL migration snippets.

sasha: Will put together a small mockup (png) and copy into the RFC thread.

kaito: I'll aim for a PoC by next Wed. Will post perf numbers for validation latency.

infra-bot: Deployment scheduled: auth/token-service will be canaried to infra-internal on 2025-07-29 03:00 UTC if CI green :rocket:

alex: Thanks all. If no objections by EOD Friday we'll lock the design and start tickets. :thumbsup:
